cycles.sequenceNote: A second lens on old history rather than a universal industrial phase. Kethra’s qualification precedes her later apprenticeship; other chapter order is provisional.

cycles.title: A Sky Full of Lives
cycles.eyebrow: Old modernity · abundance, mutual aid, aftermath
cycles.description: The magical-girl reading arc moves from everyday wonder toward the Bay and its contested aftermath; Brackenport keeps a separate clock.
cycles.sequenceNote: The subplot’s intended relative order and local sequels shape this circuit. No established date joins Brackenport, Northbridge, and every other modern-looking story.

cycles.title: The Sun’s Long Afterlife
cycles.eyebrow: Old histories · four centuries after glass
cycles.description: A regional catastrophe becomes public ritual until fractured evidence makes a second dawn possible.
cycles.sequenceNote: The Glass-Sea age is later than Nell and Bash’s modernity and the Bay. Its four centuries measure a regional history, not a global civilizational cycle.

cycles.title: The Last Convergence
cycles.eyebrow: Fixed boundary · the end of old magic
cycles.description: Thirty-one years of separate adventures converge at the Array. Six living authorities arm conditions whose release ends the old systems permanently.
cycles.sequenceNote: All old magic-active material history lies before this boundary. Similar earlier systems are not assigned to one terminal root.

cycles.title: Crowns in the Material World
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · candidate courtly civilizations
cycles.description: Creature peoples, sovereign households, adventurers, and long-lived carers need no enchantment to have histories.
cycles.sequenceNote: These are possible islands inside the magicless interval, not a single medieval age. Unusual biology and courtly appearance establish neither magic nor dates.

cycles.title: Cities Found by Hand
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · candidate craft modernities
cycles.description: Blades, engines, inherited houses, and a road beyond a five-century wall make neighboring worlds newly legible.
cycles.sequenceNote: A material-history reading circuit. The Great Wall’s five centuries are local; an illuminated city is not proof that these societies occupy successive universal rungs.

cycles.title: The Small Present
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · an ordinary civilizational island
cycles.description: Cafés, siblings, households, attraction, and private power belong within the same deep history as empires and stars.
cycles.sequenceNote: Our magicless modern time belongs inside the Long Dark. These familiar stories are candidate neighbors of that island, without a common city or exact year.

cycles.title: The City & the Synthetic Self
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · candidate engineered societies
cycles.description: Layered infrastructure and manufactured bodies make recognition, control, and personhood civic questions.
cycles.sequenceNote: Independent material modernities; no single technology ladder leads from these cities to the other circuits.

cycles.title: Worlds That Fall, Worlds That Move
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · independent falls and habitations
cycles.description: A city falls. A launch room outlives its makers. Elsewhere, rafts and living rooms remain homes by being maintained.
cycles.sequenceNote: This juxtaposes collapse and habitation without inventing successor links. Different falls may be separated by immense spans, and moving cities need not follow them.

cycles.title: The Inherited Orbit
cycles.eyebrow: The Long Dark · candidate stellar histories
cycles.description: Stations, shades, couriers, pilots, and the oldest routes carry incompatible pieces of technological deep time.
cycles.sequenceNote: The local exodus, flight incidents, and earlier stellar histories keep their own sequences. None is assigned a common launch, war, planetwide fall, or Galactic coordinate.

cycles.title: The First Reciprocal Dawn
cycles.eyebrow: Fixed boundary · new magic begins
cycles.description: Ordinary light outlives ages of perfect zero. Living people on both sides of the sky make something that did not exist before.
cycles.sequenceNote: The first link originates new magic; it restores none of the six extinct systems. The reading circuits that follow are proposals, not established descendants.

cycles.title: The Hours We Borrow
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · private impossibilities
cycles.description: Foresight, repeated time, a temporary second self, and lives carried by others open different kinds of intimate duration.
cycles.sequenceNote: A possible post-return pocket, not evidence that magic was initially secret or that time and possession share an origin. All unrelated dates remain open.

cycles.title: The Extra Place at the Table
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · domestic crossings
cycles.description: The dead, unfamiliar visitors, wings, and an infernal family complicate who may come inside and who may leave.
cycles.sequenceNote: Independent households provisionally after reawakening. They share neither an afterlife route nor one portal network.

cycles.title: Citizens of Different Bodies
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · public difference
cycles.description: Private forms meet school portraits, civil categories, hero institutions, and the practical space between lovers.
cycles.sequenceNote: A possible mature magical society circuit. Public recognition does not prove one later age, and transformation systems remain independent.

cycles.title: Gods in Company
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · authority made social
cycles.description: Gods, champions, grandmothers, and domestic villainy place immense power among people who can answer back.
cycles.sequenceNote: A separate proposed divine modernity, not the next inevitable stage after superheroes and not a universal pantheon.

cycles.title: The Roads Between Lives
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · transit and public works
cycles.description: Travel by lightning, sleep, bus, and living seams meets the obligations embedded in roads and towns.
cycles.sequenceNote: A possible integrated magical civic history. Each crossing and obligation has its own mechanism; no old network is presumed to have survived extinction.

cycles.title: Kingdoms Beneath Another Sky
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · fantasy returns as a social form
cycles.description: New kingdoms can have old buildings, customary names, restless boundaries, and difficult inheritances. Deep time makes room for fantasy after modernity.
cycles.sequenceNote: Explicitly speculative post-return homes for coordinate-open magic-active tales. Their local antiquity is not an ancient-system survival, shared ancestry, or a dated sequence.

cycles.title: The Future Has a Past
cycles.eyebrow: Proposed later history · long memory and dangerous media
cycles.description: Even a later magical world can carry millennia of private history and preserve objects or recordings it cannot safely interpret.
cycles.sequenceNote: A reading proposal for deep post-return history. The 25,000-year memory span is local; it does not date the therapy frame or establish which side of zero contains the remembered battle.

cycles.title: Clocks That Will Not Align
cycles.eyebrow: Off-axis · partial coordinates and temporal bridges
cycles.description: Ravel, a displaced village, a sequence of assignments, and a museum witness each offer a clock that cannot yet be laid flat on the worldline.
cycles.sequenceNote: Only their stated local intervals and proven endpoints are ordered. Missing coordinates are left missing rather than filled by resemblance.

cycles.title: The World Withholds an Answer
cycles.eyebrow: Off-axis · observed effects, unresolved causes
cycles.description: An inhabited colossus, a furnace crown, object memories, medicinal plants, night creatures, and a higher-order machine expose the limits of easy labels.
cycles.sequenceNote: Mechanism-open tales remain outside an asserted old/new/zero assignment. Measurements and practical repairs do not prove that an effect is exclusively nonmagical.

cycles.title: Rooms Beside the Worldline
cycles.eyebrow: Off-axis · living voices and other ontologies
cycles.description: A constructed-life school, an inherited pendant, a divine family, and arrivals beyond ordinary material life keep their own unsettled relation to history.
cycles.sequenceNote: The active powers and off-world frames here are not exceptions inside the Long Dark. Their material coordinates, era sides, and connections remain unestablished.

connections.label: The light that reaches another sky
connections.note: The established chronology and return story continue Faris and Seyathi’s final fall, then follow ordinary light across ages of perfect zero. Their deaths remain final and no old system returns.

connections.label: One world, a later age
connections.note: The established chronology places Nell and Bash’s old-modern endpoint long before the Glass-Sea era on the same physical world. This orders that endpoint only; Ravel remains undated.

connections.label: The world survives to the Glass Sea
connections.note: The established western-bay chronology places Solstice’s battle before the later Glass-Sea era. No common magical system or measured interval is established.

connections.label: Three afternoons later
connections.note: The Help Network opens at Northbridge on the third afternoon after the showcase, with Cassia, Drita, and Bryn building on the earlier channel compromise.

connections.label: Mutual aid before the Bay
connections.note: The intended reading sequence sets The Help Network after The Attendance Ledger and before Solstice Evening Bell. This is an editorial sequence, with no established date or institutional ancestry.

connections.label: A crowded sky, then the Bay
connections.note: The intended reading sequence locates Not About That before Solstice, when magical girls are numerous. Its order relative to Northbridge remains open.

connections.label: The aftermath misidentifies a survivor
connections.note: The intended reading sequence places Dress after Solstice and before Count. Its damaged post-battle institutions turn ordinary booking marks into a false survivor claim. The prisoner is not Solstice.

connections.label: From misidentification to misremembrance
connections.note: The subplot’s intended reading sequence places Dress between Solstice and Count, without an established interval. The prisoner and the later museum witness are different people.

connections.label: The witness corrects the count
connections.note: The museum prose explicitly identifies its living witness as Solstice Evening Bell, centuries after the same Battle of the Bay. The museum’s side of extinction remains unknown.

connections.label: The archmage becomes a teacher
connections.note: Voice establishes Kethra’s qualification; Lock begins with the same named archmage taking a mistreated apprentice and uses her call-link practice. The interval is not dated.

connections.label: Two arrangements for twelve dragons
connections.note: Indirect parallel only: Kharost’s rotating Crown offices and Varkesh’s collective Sleepless Majesty make different bargains with governance and sleep. No common cast, state, or sequel is established.

connections.label: A home is also a living body
connections.note: Agnes exposes coerced structural labor; Lirenn discovers occupied volume inside living leased rooms. The ethical echo crosses proposed eras without asserting shared biology or building lineage.

connections.label: Who can claim a memory?
connections.note: One-use sensory fragments from retrieved objects and licensed neural extraction make distinct memory problems. The resemblance is thematic, not a shared substance or technological ancestry.

connections.label: The record beneath the monument
connections.note: A museum’s heroic reconstruction and a drowned-king interpretation meet more limited evidence. This is a reader parallel about misremembered history, not a common archive.

connections.label: Humanity becomes an inheritance
connections.note: A dinosaur surface polity and a later stellar courier encounter different human legacies. No common departure, station network, or absolute order is established.

connections.label: Learning what the creatures actually do
connections.note: Route observations change how people respond to shadow beasts and throat-node-bearing creatures. The stories establish no common species, invasion, or mechanism.

connections.label: A useful organism changes the question
connections.note: Both communities must reconsider handling practices after observing effects. The slime’s material behavior does not classify the Night Harvest effect or date either settlement.

connections.label: When the ground stops being a promise
connections.note: Evacuation requires precise counts when an inhabited hand moves and when Orison loses lift. The colossus is not assigned a reactor cause; these are not the same fall.

connections.label: The past arrives in a new present
connections.note: An intact displaced village and genetically reconstructed adults confront later institutions. Actual temporal transport and reconstruction remain different processes, not one refounding event.

connections.label: A person falls outside the map
connections.note: A threshold working disrupts a public road; a networked city cannot place an unregistered passenger. The people, technologies, and causes differ, despite the shared recognition problem.

connections.label: The destination keeps its own clock
connections.note: An assignment sequence and the Ravel encounter both resist a flat timeline. Their resemblance proves neither one portal network nor that Ryo’s destinations are Ravel.

connections.label: Crossings bring obligations home
connections.note: Bearer-powered sanctuary crossings and a living market seam both impose local limits. No mechanism, underworld, or ancient route is shared by implication.

connections.label: Company at a threshold
connections.note: Borrowed living hosts and a stranded afterlife traveler create different obligations to another person. The parallel establishes no common possession or station mechanism.

connections.label: A political offer needs a person’s answer
connections.note: Royal negotiation meets the independent will of the people inside it. This is an ethical parallel between unrelated courts, not a dynasty or a continuation of Ninepin.

connections.label: What the inherited promise costs
connections.note: A solar polity and a witch’s town confront responsibilities accumulated over generations. The juxtaposition does not make promise-binding a descendant of solar fire.

connections.label: A name that can be chosen
connections.note: Different pressures around names and identity invite a joint reading. The stories do not share a name-magic rule, heroic lineage, or cast.

connections.label: One family, unequal capacities
connections.note: An elf caregiver and the mortal eldest of a divine household feel limits differently from those around them. Longevity is not treated as proof that the two families occupy the same era.
